footer.tagline: Designed, built, and flown by Alejandro Valdez.

valdex.tagline: Flight computers and telemetry, designed and built in-house.
valdex.overview: Valdex LLC is my engineering company focused on designing and manufacturing avionics hardware for high-power rocketry. Every board is designed in KiCad, fabricated, hand-assembled, and flown.
valdex.detail1: Custom ARM-based flight computer with barometric altimeter, IMU, and dual-deploy pyrotechnic outputs. Designed for reliability under 20G launch loads.
valdex.detail2: LoRa-based ground station with live GPS tracking, altitude plotting, and recovery beacon. Range tested to 8km line-of-sight.
valdex.detail3: Real-time telemetry dashboard built in Python with live map integration, sensor graphs, and flight replay. The Valdex Telemetry Suite.

restem.tagline: Real engineering, in the hands of the next generation.
restem.overview: ReSTEM is a nonprofit I founded to close the gap between students with big ideas and the real engineering education they need to pursue them.
restem.detail1: Hands-on workshops, rocketry builds, electronics projects, and engineering design challenges that put real tools in students' hands.
restem.detail2: Partnerships with Central Florida schools, libraries, and engineering professionals. 200+ students reached, focused on underrepresented communities.
restem.detail3: Not just showing students slides, we build. Every program ends with something the student made themselves.

sunflower.tagline: Flown at Spaceport America. Open source down to the last screw.
sunflower.overview: Sunflower is the SHPE UCF payload that flew and competed at the 2026 ESRA Intercollegiate Rocket Engineering Competition. I co-led the build end to end: structure, sensor electronics, and the ESP-IDF flight firmware. The full design, code, and bill of materials are open source.
sunflower.detail1: Atmospheric data collection at apogee, pressure, temperature, humidity, and particulate sampling during the 10,000-ft ascent and descent.
sunflower.detail2: Aluminum payload bay with custom PCB sensor array, onboard data logging, and passive thermal management for high-altitude exposure.
sunflower.detail3: ESP-IDF on FreeRTOS with a flight state machine. IMU sampling runs at high priority, tracking at medium, and logging at low, so sensor data is never dropped during boost.

odysseus.tagline: Ten thousand feet. Built by students, engineered like a flagship.
odysseus.overview: Odysseus is UCF's competition vehicle for the 2026 Intercollegiate Rocket Engineering Competition. A full-scale, student-designed and built rocket targeting 10,000 ft AGL under FAA and NAR safety frameworks.
odysseus.detail1: Commercial high-power motor with custom forward and aft airframe integration. Motor selection optimized for target apogee under competition weight budget.
odysseus.detail2: Fiberglass and carbon fiber composite airframe with machined aluminum couplers. Designed for structural integrity through transonic flight regime.
odysseus.detail3: Dual-deploy recovery with Valdex custom flight computer as primary, commercial altimeter as backup. Full telemetry from pad to recovery.

fsi.tagline: Research at the edge of Florida's space coast.
fsi.overview: The Florida Space Institute at UCF is one of Florida's premier space research centers. Work here connects directly to real aerospace engineering projects and research initiatives.
fsi.detail1: Aerospace systems engineering with emphasis on small satellite subsystems, propulsion analysis, and mission design methodology.
fsi.detail2: Working alongside graduate researchers, faculty, and industry partners on projects with real mission relevance.
fsi.detail3: Research outputs contribute to ongoing FSI initiatives and support UCF's growing role in Florida's commercial space ecosystem.

monkeybar.tagline: Launch it. Land it. Aim it. A two-stage guided rocket.
monkeybar.overview: Monkey Bar sets out to launch, land, and aim a rocket. The booster carries two thrust vector control mounts to land under control, while the upper stage, Dart, uses canard fins to hit a ground target, scored on accuracy over speed. A Yagi-linked ground station and a dedicated launch system round out the program.
monkeybar.detail1: Two stages. The booster uses dual TVC mounts for a controlled landing; Dart uses canards to steer onto a target for a measurable yield.
monkeybar.detail2: Live onboard data over a Yagi antenna link, giving the team real-time safety visibility through every phase.
monkeybar.detail3: Reliable launch, a clean landing site for the booster, and a safe range to measure where Dart lands.

phantom.tagline: Mission control for a Mach 1 attempt.
phantom.overview: A native desktop ground station built for the Boom Prize: the first amateur RC aircraft to exceed Mach 1, twice, on the same day. It ingests live LoRa telemetry over USB serial, or runs the real mission profile in simulation, behind one source interface so the dashboard, alerts, and abort logic never change.
phantom.detail1: Mach as the largest element on screen, plus airspeed, altitude, attitude, dynamic pressure with a redline, GPS ground track, G-load, and propulsion health.
phantom.detail2: An armed or abort kill-switch indicator, fault injection for rehearsal, checklists, and alerts that behave identically in simulation and live flight.
phantom.detail3: A versioned key=value serial format with CRC-16 checks and a reference encoder the firmware team builds against, testable end to end without hardware.

vxtelemetry.tagline: Plug in any flight computer. Watch the mission unfold live.
vxtelemetry.overview: VX Telemetry is the flagship Valdex product: hardware-agnostic ground-station software for high-power rocketeers and competition teams up to L3. It recognizes incoming streams automatically, and flies your own CAD model live from telemetry attitude.
vxtelemetry.detail1: Mission clock, flight-phase track from pad to landing, a GO/NO-GO board, drag-aware apogee prediction, and touchdown ETA.
vxtelemetry.detail2: Upload your own rocket CAD and watch it fly from live attitude data, with staging, drogue, and main deployment animated from real flight events.
vxtelemetry.detail3: An NDJSON frame contract with automatic alias mapping and an in-app field mapper. Third-party firmware works with no code changes. Also supports TVC, canard, and air brake telemetry.

harper.tagline: The road to Level 1. Two attempts, one rocket philosophy.
harper.overview: Harper is my Level 1 high-power certification rocket. The first attempt, flown on an H169, did not earn the certification. Every lesson from that flight is going into attempt two.
harper.detail1: The first design and first flight on an H169 motor. It did not certify. Fill in at /admin: what happened and what you learned.

about.intro: Aerospace engineering student at UCF. I learn by building: avionics, flight software, rockets, and the teams behind them. Founder of Valdex LLC and the ReSTEM nonprofit.

Built the Phantom mission-control app for a Mach 1 RC aircraft attempt.
